procedures: 1. Investigate for prominent physical damage to any components before proceeding. This may include wires with damaged insulation, dents or large cracks visible on components, or missing wires 2. Locate the power distribution and diagnostic (PDD) component by identifying an irregular-shaped white housing labeled with 'PDD9900xxxx' 3. On the PDD display, verify the vehicle is in recovery mode and not some other error state, this is indicated by the error code 4800 and a red light by the recovery switch, labeled 'RECO' 4. If a different error is displayed, that error must be fixed prior to exiting recovery mode 5. Via the Power Override Panel for Subsystems, labeled 'POPS', move switches for 'MPS', 'GNC', and 'CDH' to the 'OFF' position 6. Locate the Software Fault Acknowledge button, labeled 'SFA' 7. Press and release the SFA button 8. Move the Power Optimization Mode switch, labeled 'POM', to the 'OFF' position, verify change by confirming a blue indicator light 9. Open the switch cover for the External Battery Disconnect switch, labeled 'EBD' 10. Press and hold the Computer Software Reboot button, labeled 'CSR' 11. While holding the CSR button, move the EBD switch to the 'ON' position 12. Release the CSR button 13. Identify the Software Management and Control (SMC) component by identifying a rectangular white housing labeled with 'SMC1100xxxx'. Wait 5-10 seconds for the reboot to take effect. Successful reboot will be indicated by the green light on the software management box turning on 14. Move the EBD switch to the 'OFF' position 15. Close the EBD switch cover 16. Verify the red status light on the SMC begins blinking 17. Via POPS, move the switches for MPS, GNC, and CDH to the 'ON' position 18. Open the switch cover for the control switch, labeled 'CTRL', on the SMC 19. On the SMC, press and hold the black alternative button, labeled 'ALT', while moving the CTRL switch to the on position 20. Verify the red status light on the SMC turns off 21. Release the ALT button 22. Test the reboot by pushing the 'TEST' switch upward on the SMC and pressing and holding the CSR button on the PDD 23. Once the green status light on the SMC begins blinking, release the CSR button 24. On the SMC, press and hold the black ALT button while switching the CTRL switch to the 'OFF' position 25. Verify a solid green status light has illuminated 26. Release the black ALT button and close the switch cover of the CTRL switch 27. On the PDD, open the switch cover for the recovery switch, labeled 'RECO' 28. Move the RECO switch to the 'OFF' position and close the cover 29. Verify the LTV has exited recovery mode by confirming the error code 4800 no longer displays and the RECO indicator light is no longer illuminated 30. Announce ERM success

error_procedures.description: NAV Restart & Manual Return to Home
procedures: 1. Locate the Navigation Control Panel (NAV) by identifying a rectangular white housing labeled 'NAV5500xxxx' 2. Move the primary control switch under the green light to the far left, entering 'HAND' mode. Verify mode switch by confirming the mode indicator light turns blue 3. Identify the 'LIDAR RESET' button 4. Flush and restart the LIDAR system by pressing and holding this button for 5 seconds. The LIDAR button indicator will light red upon depressing this button 5. On the SMC, once the green status light has illuminated, release the LIDAR Reset button 6. On the NAV component, Identify the 'NAV RESET' button  7. Flush and restart the NAV System by pressing and holding this button for 5 seconds. The NAV button indicator will light red upon depressing this button 8. On the SMC, once the red indicator light has illuminated, release the NAV Restart Button 9. On the NAV component, enact the reset by moving the primary control switch to the 'OFF' position and wait for 5 seconds 10. Move the primary control switch to HAND mode 11. Verify mode switch by confirming the mode indicator light is blue 12. Identify the autonomous systems indicator toggle switch labeled 'ASITS' 13. Move the ASITS switch to the 'ON' position 14. Verify mode switch by confirming the indicator light is yellow and the remaining indicators are on 15. Identify the autonomous navigation system lock labeled 'ANAV BLOCK' 16. Move this switch to the 'ON' position, verify mode switch by confirming the indicator light is blue 17. Identify the manual return to home switch labeled 'ANAV RTH' 18. Move this switch to the 'ON' position, verify mode switch by confirming the indicator light is blue 19. Identify the autonomy confidence adjustment dial labeled 'ACA' 20. Rotate this dial counterclockwise to manually reduce the confidence scale of the autonomous navigation algorithm until the light is red 21. Move the ANAV BLOCK switch to the 'OFF' position 22. Move the ASITS switch to the 'OFF' position 23. Identify the autonomous Cognitive Obstacle and Motion Manager switch, labeled 'COMM' 24. Turn the switch to the 'SEC' position, and verify mode switch by confirming the indicator light is blue 25. On the SMC, verify the status lights have turned off 26. Move the primary control switch to the 'AUTO' position, verify mode switch by confirming mode indicator light is green 27. Announce successful NAV Restart & Manual Return to Home steps complete

1. Locate the Backup Fuse Housing by identifying a rectangular gray housing labeled 'BFH9900xxxx' 2. Lift the lid of the enclosure, exposing a black protective barrier, ensure the lid locks in the upright position 3. Before proceeding, be cognizant of sharp edges, pinch points, and where necessary, hold the enclosure steady with one hand while performing the following steps 4. Remove the fuse disconnect by pulling the exposed black handle located towards the top of the box, moderate force may be required 5. Remove the protective barrier by pulling upward from the opening marked by the 'PULL' label 6. Use the provided fuse-puller tool to safely remove both fuses and properly discard them 7. Locate the replacement fuses 8. Using the fuse-puller tool, place a new fuse in the grips of the tool 9. Insert the fuse into the empty slot, moderate force may be required 10. Repeat steps 7 and 8 for the other fuse 11. Replace the black protective barrier 12. Reinsert the fuse disconnect in the proper orientation 13. Close the lid of the enclosure by lifting slightly upwards and pulling down 14. Announce Backup Fuse Error resolved

1. Locate the antenna calibration and modification (ACM) component by identifying a square gray housing labeled 'ACM4400xxxx' 2. Locate the phase control knob, labeled 'PHS', rotate this until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 3. Locate the modulation control knob, labeled 'MOD', rotate until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 4. Locate the amplitude control knob, labeled 'AMP', rotate until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 5. If the green indicator has not been lit, you may rotate these controls until maximum RSSI strength has been achieved, this is indicated by the green indicator being lit 6. Announce Poor Comms RSSI error resolved

1. On the PDD, via POPS, move switches for 'MPS', 'GNC', 'VSI', and 'CDH' to the 'OFF' position 2. Check for any loose bus cables 3. If a cable is deemed loose, fully remove the cable from its socket 4. Firmly reinsert the cable into its socket 5. If no cable is deemed loose, fully remove and reinsert each cable into the respective sockets 6. Via POPS, move switches for 'MPS', 'GNC', 'VSI', and 'CDH' to the 'ON' position 7. Wait 5-10 seconds to verify the error clears before proceeding 8. Announce Subsystem Power Bus error resolved

1. On the PDD, via the Power Override Panel for Subsystems, labeled 'POPS', move the Command and Data Handling switch, labeled 'CDH' to the 'OFF' position 2. Wait 5 seconds 3. Move the CDH switch to the 'ON' position 4. Locate the antenna communications control component by identifying a square gray box with white turn knobs and a strip of indicator lights 5. If maximum RSSI strength is not indicated, proceed with the following steps 6. Locate the phase control knob, labeled 'PHS', rotate this until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 7. Locate the modulation control knob, labeled 'MOD', rotate until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 8. Locate the amplitude control knob, labeled 'AMP', rotate until maximum possible RSSI improvement is achieved 9. If the green indicator has not been lit, you may rotate these controls until maximum RSSI strength has been achieved, this is indicated by the green indicator being lit 10. On the SMC, verify the red status light has begun blinking 11. On SMC, press and hold the black ALT button while flipping the CTRL switch to the 'ON' position 12. Once the red status light is no longer illuminated, release the ALT button 13. To finish resetting the software for the ACM, press and hold the black ALT button and the red RESET button at the same time 14. Verify both red and green status lights illuminate, indicating a successful reset 15. Release both buttons 16. To test the software reboot, push the 'TEST' switch downwards until the green status light begins blinking. If the green status light is not blinking after 20 seconds, announce green light not blinking 17. Hold down the black ALT button while moving the CTRL switch to the 'OFF' position 18. Release the black ALT button and close the cover on the CTRL switch 19. Verify the green status light has illuminated, indicating successful test 20. Announce Comms Reboot steps complete

1. Locate the dust sensor by identifying a cylindrical white housing smaller than the palm of a hand 2. Rotate the sensor body counterclockwise to unscrew it from its base 3. Once removed, set the sensor aside 4. Locate the replacement sensor and twist the protective cap counterclockwise to remove it, this cap may be put on the broken dust sensor 5. Insert the replacement sensor into the base and rotate clockwise until firmly secured 6. Announce Dust Sensor error resolved

1. Locate the Scientific Management and Power Distribution (SMPD) component by identifying a gray rectangular housing labeled 'SMPD2200xxxx' 2. Verify the SMPD indicator light is illuminated green, an unlit indicator implies an upstream power distribution issue and must be resolved first. Refer to the PDD display for which error is indicated 3. Locate the Scientific Power Regulation (SPR) component by identifying a small black housing labeled 'SPR2200xxxx' 4. Take note of any illuminated red indicator lights on the SPR and their position 5. On the PDD, via POPS, move the Mission Payload Subsystem switch, labeled 'MPS' to the 'OFF' position 6. To prevent damage from unexpected electrical surges during operation, remove the power bus from its socket before proceeding 7. On the SPR, corresponding to the side that had an illuminated indicator, locate the fuse cartridge for that side and remove it 2. Prepare and insert a replacement fuse cartridge into the empty section 3. On the PDD, via POPS, reinsert the power bus 4. Move the MPS switch to the 'ON' position 5. Verify the SMPD indicator is illuminated green and no indicators are illuminated on the SPR 6. Announce Scientific Power Distribution steps complete
